name: Rizpah
bio: Rizpah was the daughter of Aiah, a concubine of Saul. After Saul's death, Ish-Bosheth confronted Abner over sleeping with her, a charge Abner took as an accusation of coveting the throne; infuriated, he defected to David instead — a turning point that reshaped the balance of power between the two rival houses (2 Samuel 3:7-11). Years later, a three-year famine struck Israel, and the LORD revealed it was because Saul had broken Israel's covenant oath to the Gibeonites by trying to annihilate them. To make atonement, David handed over seven of Saul's male descendants for the Gibeonites to execute — including Rizpah's own two sons, Armoni and Mephibosheth — and they were hanged before the LORD at the beginning of the barley harvest (2 Samuel 21:1-9). Rizpah then took sackcloth and spread it on a rock for herself, keeping watch over the bodies from the start of harvest until the autumn rains finally fell, refusing to let birds by day or wild animals by night come near them. When David heard what she had done, he was moved to recover the long-unburied bones of Saul and Jonathan as well, and gave the bones of all of Saul's family a proper burial in the family tomb — after which, Scripture notes, "God answered prayer on behalf of the land" (2 Samuel 21:10-14). Rizpah's silent, months-long vigil, demanding nothing but simply refusing to let her sons' bodies be further dishonored, stands as one of Scripture's most powerful portraits of a grieving mother's fierce, enduring love.
